_comment: Development realm for AI WorkOS. Imported by the Compose `keycloak` service at start-up
(`start-dev --import-realm`). For running the stack by hand only: the test suite never starts
Keycloak, it signs its own tokens with a throwaway RSA key and stubs the JWKS endpoint
(testing-strategy T-3, resolved as option (a)). Production code validates identically either
way — issuer, audience, expiry and signature.
One realm serves every organization (PQ-2, ADR-0031). There is deliberately no organization
claim anywhere below: membership is resolved from local rows, because a claim would keep
asserting a membership after it was revoked (security-model §2).
Every secret and password here is a development placeholder and is meant to be visible.

realm.name: workos-user
realm.description: Can sign in to AI WorkOS. Carries no authority of its own: every permission that matters comes from RoleAssignment rows in the application database (security-model §2).

clients.name: AI WorkOS web application
clients.description: First-party SPA. Authorization code with PKCE, no client secret, access token held in memory only.

clients.name: AI WorkOS API
clients.description: The resource server. Bearer-only: it is the audience tokens are checked against, never an issuer of them.

clients.name: Channel connector (Phase 2)
clients.description: Client-credentials service account for the ingestion API. Holds ingestion rights only and must never be able to reach the Tool Gateway (ADR-0027): a compromised channel may inject content but may not act on it. Unused until Phase 2.

clientScopes.name: workos-audience
clientScopes.description: Puts `workos-api` in the `aud` claim. Without it every token would be rejected, because audience is one of the four things the API checks on every request.
